title: Nepal's Prisons Overcrowded by 43%, Management Department Initiates Measures - Ratopati
description: Nepal's Prisons Overcrowded by 43%, Management Department Initiates Measures  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
There are 73 prisons across the country. Currently, there are a total of 27,798 inmates in all prisons in Nepal. The number of inmates in prison is 43 percent more than the capacity of the prison. Although there has been a long-standing debate about reducing the pressure of inmates, the pressure has not decreased.

The Department of Prison Management under the Ministry of Home Affairs has been working to reduce the pressure of inmates in prisons and build physical structures. However, with the physical structure construction happening at a snail's pace, it seems it will take many years to reduce the pressure.

The Council of Ministers has initiated efforts to reduce the pressure of inmates by issuing a new prison regulation this year. Edited excerpt of the conversation between Ratopati correspondent Rajesh Bhandari and department director Chomendra Neupane about the efforts to reduce the pressure of inmates and increase infrastructure:

The department's own statistics show that prisons are currently 43 percent overcrowded. How are you managing the excessive pressure of inmates?

Yes, prisons are currently 43 percent more overcrowded than their capacity. Our prisons have been suffering from problems of dilapidation, narrowness, and lack of space for a long time. The work of establishing new prisons has started in the last few years. We have thought of managing the pressure of inmates in a few ways.

Some prisons also have fewer inmates than their capacity. We have managed by transferring inmates from prisons with more inmates than capacity to prisons with fewer inmates in some cases. We are also constructing new infrastructure simultaneously. We have advanced the construction of 6-7 prisons in the last fiscal year. We are moving forward with the master plan to expand the capacity of large prisons like Naubasta and Nuwakot.

In addition, a budget has been allocated in this fiscal year for the construction of new infrastructure in 12 more prisons. We are moving forward with the work of expanding the capacity by constructing new infrastructure and also by maintaining the existing prisons.

To manage the number of prisoners and foster a sense of ownership towards the state among prisoners, we have provided the facility of sentence reduction. Prisoners working as watchmen, naike, and saha-naike in the internal administration of the jail receive a reduction of 6, 5, and 4 days per month, respectively. The Department of Prison Management has been providing this facility.

Similarly, inmates are released from prison through the facility of parole as an alternative to imprisonment. This has also helped reduce the pressure of inmates in prisons. Previously, sentence reduction and amnesty had reduced the pressure of inmates. Sentence reduction and amnesty have been stopped for the last two years.

Overall, the number of undertrials is also excessive. If the judicial process is completed in time, the period of pre-trial detention will decrease, and the number of prisoners will be reduced. Elderly citizens have also not been released for some years. The sentence reduction regulation has not been implemented for two years, and elderly citizens have not been released due to pending cases in court. If the sentence reduction facility of up to 75 percent available to senior citizens is provided, it will be possible to reduce the pressure of inmates in prison.

What efforts are being made to expand the capacity of prisons? Where is the capacity being expanded?

Currently, the capacity of the Central Prison built in Nuwakot is being expanded. We have proposed to expand the capacity of Jhapa Prison. A budget has been allocated to expand the capacity of Naubasta in Banke, and we will move forward with it chronologically.

In the previous fiscal year, the third phase of construction work for the prisons in Panchthar, Rasuwa, Naubasta, Mugu, Humla, Surkhet, Bajhang, and Nuwakot was underway, and work was also being done in Jajarkot, Bajura, and Baitadi. In the current fiscal year, a budget has been allocated to construct some new prisons. A budget has been allocated to complete the plans from the previous year in some prisons. Work will proceed in 20 prisons this time.

In the past, the budget allocated to prisons was relatively low. This year, we have increased the scope of budget allocation and are working on construction to accommodate a large number of inmates in prisons with excessive inmate populations. Along with this, we can reduce the pressure of inmates by transferring, providing sentence reduction facilities, and coordinating with the courts for faster resolution of pre-trial cases.

What is the status of the implementation of parole, a new initiative in the prison system, to reduce the pressure of inmates?

Parole is a legal provision stipulated in Section 29 of the Fugitive Offenses Sentencing and Implementation Act, 2074. It is a provision for releasing inmates who have been sentenced to more than one year in prison, have served two-thirds of their sentence, and have good conduct on parole. Parole is not granted to defendants in 10 negative list cases such as life imprisonment, corruption, rape, and human trafficking. The Federal Parole Board has decided not to release those involved in inhumane and cruel torture under wildlife, counterfeit currency, and murder cases. Parole is also not granted if a life has been taken by reversing a vehicle under vehicular homicide.

The parole system started on Poush 25, 2080. So far, the Federal Parole Board has held 17 meetings and released 2900 inmates. Some child molesters have also been released among them.

Only 3 percent of the inmates released on parole, having agreed to the terms of the parole board, have violated the conditions while living at home. This is very low. The success rate of parole is very high. The number of inmates who do not re-offend after being released or do not appear at the scheduled time is minimal.

The provision for inmates to mingle before completing their sentence after serving two-thirds of their sentence with good conduct, engage in their professions, live with their families, and utilize their productive age has also created a sense of ownership towards the state. The state can also benefit from their contributions.

How is the concept of open prisons being implemented? What are the provisions regarding open prisons in the recently issued Prison Regulation 083?

Open prisons have been introduced as per the provisions of the Fugitive Offenses Sentencing Act. It has a provision for keeping individuals who have served two-thirds of their sentence and have good conduct in open prisons. The Prison Act 2079 also has provisions for open prisons. According to the act, an open prison is defined as any place designated by the Government of Nepal where inmates can go outside their designated place of confinement to perform work.

Accordingly, inmates in open prisons have the facility to work outside the designated place. Rule 45 of the newly issued Prison Regulation 2083 states that the Government of Nepal can designate any building or place within Nepal as an open prison as needed. This will be implemented only after the building or place is designated by a notice published in the Nepal Gazette. This provision is in the Fugitive Offenses Sentencing Act.

To designate an open prison, adequate infrastructure, budget, security arrangements, available services and facilities, and criteria for the type of individuals to be housed there need to be prepared. According to the Prison Act and Fugitive Offenses Sentencing Act, inmates residing in open prisons can be employed. The Government of Nepal can also employ them in factories opened within the premises.

According to our legal provisions, inmates in open prisons and special prisons must be kept within those respective prisons. They cannot be transferred to other prisons. Therefore, even during transfers, we must take inmates from open prisons to open prisons. Hence, before declaring an open prison, the place of work and the prison for transfer must be managed. Because if something happens there and they need to be moved elsewhere, an open prison will be needed again. The government can designate open prisons for establishing factories, agricultural farms, or animal husbandry. It is not yet clear how open prisons will be designated.

According to our legal provisions, inmates can also be employed in federal or provincial projects designated by the government. They can be employed as volunteers or kept in open prisons for training. However, preparation is required for this.

The new regulation includes provisions for collecting inmate applications, sending them to the Open Prison Management Committee through the department, and after their recommendation, sending them to the concerned court for action as per the court's order. Security arrangements for open prisons also need to be specified. We are in the preparation phase regarding how to proceed with this.

What is the concept of taking inmates who have served two-thirds of their sentence outside prison to work? How is it possible?

Individuals who have served two-thirds of their sentence and have good conduct are placed in open prisons. They can be employed in federal projects. Inmates who have served two-thirds of their sentence are also released on parole. The sentence reduction regulation, which has been halted for two years, is in the process of amendment. Now, only those on the negative list will not be released after serving two-thirds of their sentence. These are individuals involved in those 10 types of cases. The number of people who can be employed in projects is limited to them. That number may be small.

Therefore, to accommodate a larger number of inmates, it would be more effective if those who have completed even 50 percent of their sentence could also be kept in open prisons and employed in projects. This will be discussed, as it has just come into the regulation.

And what are the reform measures within prisons in the new regulation?

Even when the Prison Act 2079 was enacted, the Prison Regulation 2020 was still in effect. Now, the Prison Regulation 2083 has been issued, incorporating provisions relevant to the current times. In prisons, activities like making stools, carpets, bangles, spinning yarn, and handicrafts have been ongoing. To systematize this, the new regulation includes the establishment of entrepreneurship centers. Entrepreneurship centers can be registered with the department by creating specific procedures. A separate naike will be appointed to operate these entrepreneurship centers. Private sector factories will now be able to open branches in prisons. In such factories, inmates will get work, and the products will have market access.

The use of the Prison Management Information System has been made mandatory to make prison management IT-friendly. Through this system, information about inmates and their status in prisons is transmitted to the department. The current regulation includes provisions for securing the biometric details of inmates. The regulation also systematizes visiting arrangements and the conditions that inmates must adhere to.

Inmates do not need to be physically present in court for deposition. In the new regulation, deposition can be conducted virtually through coordination with the relevant court.

Previously, inmates were provided with blankets once every two years. Now, the provision of providing one blanket each year has been implemented. The festival allowance has been increased to 500 rupees.

Health insurance was not available before, but it has been included now. Rule 26 of the regulation provides for the right to conjugal visits for husband and wife to protect reproductive rights. The concerned prison must facilitate this arrangement. If the couple will be over 40 years old upon release from prison, we must provide a separate room to protect their reproductive rights.

When appointing individuals for internal administration, the provision is to appoint those with qualifications and capabilities through a committee recommendation. The coordinator of the recommendation committee will be the Chief District Officer or a person designated by them.

To reduce complaints about exorbitant fees for consumables in prisons, the department can sign an agreement with the Food Management and Trading Company for the supply of goods and services at subsidized rates. A provision has been made to establish counters of companies supplying goods and services in prisons, from where goods and services can be provided at subsidized rates.

A provision has been made to open accounts for inmates so that the services and facilities provided by the government go directly into their accounts. A committee led by the Chief District Officer has been formed to control the situation where influential individuals get health check-ups at private hospitals. Inmates can only be sent to private hospitals upon the recommendation of this committee.

Furthermore, security arrangements and the duties of security personnel are separately mentioned. The role of the Chief District Officer in the context of prisons is also clarified in the regulation. The duties of the jailer are also clearly mentioned in the regulation. The provision for sentence reduction for special responsibilities has also been systematized, as there was some ambiguity before. Also, the provision to allow inmates to travel up to 10 kilometers with the permission of the Chief District Officer for attending funerals has been included.

How are reproductive rights being managed? When will inmates receive that right?

This provision has been made to protect human rights and for individuals who do not have children. The idea is that if the husband or wife will be over 40 years of age upon release from prison, this facility should be provided to the inmate. Separate rooms need to be established to implement this.

Currently, with the lack of space for sleeping and living in prisons, it is not possible to implement the right to conjugal visits in all prisons at once. Therefore, structures need to be built. We will gradually build rooms based on the available space in the prisons.

We have already established a location in Doti for reproductive rights. Individuals can be sent to Doti to avail this facility if they apply for reproductive rights. We will build structures wherever possible. We will provide the facility by transferring eligible inmates who request it. We will construct prison structures with dedicated rooms in new locations.

Why are individuals up to 35 years old who have committed child sexual abuse kept in juvenile correction homes?

This is regulated by the Children's Act. It is due to the legal provision that individuals who have completed 18 years of age should be kept separately from those who have not. We have recently separated those above 18 years from those below 18 years. For example, in Morang, we have kept those above 18 years separately. We have also kept those above 18 years separately in Nuwakot after transferring them from Bhaktapur. Those above 18 years have also been kept separately in Naubasta. The practice of separating them gradually has been initiated. This has reduced clashes in juvenile correction homes. However, the law needs to be clear on whether individuals who have completed 18 years should be kept in prison or not. If the law allows them to be kept in prison after reaching the age of majority, then they can be kept in prison.

KATHMANDU, AUGUST 17

The dissident faction of the Nepali Congress, led by Sher Bahadur Deuba, concluded a three-day national gathering in Kathmandu today, adopting five major political resolutions on the party's upcoming 15th General Convention, constitutional amendments, and national identity in terms of religion and culture.

Related Articles Nepali Congress edges towards formal split SC legitimizes special general convention of Nepali Congress

The gathering began on August 14, and while it formally concluded on schedule, one resolution - on religion and culture - sparked serious discussion and, ultimately, an on-stage dispute among senior leaders. On religious policy, the assembly committed to recognising Sanatan traditions as a defining aspect of Nepal's national identity.

The resolution read: "Nepal's traditional religion and culture since ancient times is also our national identity. Considering the duty to protect Hindu, Buddhist, Kirat and Prakriti religions... the commitment will be made to move the nation forward with Sanatan religion as the national identity."

Despite the gathering's formal conclusion, its final session was marred by a public dispute between senior leaders on stage over the wording of this resolution. As leader Deepak Prasad Kuikel read out the drafted resolutions from the rostrum, former vice-president Bimalendra Nidhi approached the lectern to object to the draft prepared by former spokesperson Dr Prakash Sharan Mahat. A brief physical scuffle followed as the two leaders tugged over the draft document before Dr Mahat escorted Nidhi back to his seat.

The disagreement centred on specific phrasing. Dr Mahat's draft advocated recognising Sanatan traditions as part of the national identity while guaranteeing freedom to practise historical faiths. Nidhi argued that the party should adhere strictly to its traditional stance of 'religious freedom', without additional qualification.

Deuba ultimately intervened, directing that Dr Mahat's original draft be read out as written. Addressing the assembly, he said that while he personally identifies as Hindu, he fully respects the freedom of all individuals to practise their respective faiths. "I am personally a Hindu," Deuba said in his address to party cadres. "I have observed the Bratabandha sacred thread ceremony and married according to Hindu traditions. I visit Pashupatinath and offer prayers."

Addressing broader state policy and constitutional issues concerning religion, he emphasised that ultimate authority rests with the sovereign public rather than political decrees. "However, what happens or does not happen in terms of religion in the country depends on the decision of the people," Deuba stated, adding, "There must be religious freedom for everyone in the nation."

According to the second resolution, the assembly decided that the 15th General Convention will be organised under Deuba's leadership and direction, with Dr Shashank Koirala appointed chief coordinator. The faction expressed firm confidence that unifying the party under Deuba's leadership is critical to the convention's success and in the meantime, Koirala will coordinate regular party activities under Deuba's direction.

The third resolution urged dialogue with national and democratic forces to strengthen nationalism and democratic institutions, citing BP Koirala's 1976 policy of national unity and reconciliation during times of crisis. The fourth resolution commits to pursuing necessary constitutional amendments through dialogue with relevant stakeholders within the current constitutional framework.

THAPA WARNS AGAINST PRIVATISING LEGACY OF LEADERS

Nepali Congress (NC) President Gagan Kumar Thapa cautioned that the legacy of leaders such as BP Koirala and Ganeshman Singh should not be ''privatised'' or confined to their families, stressing that their political contributions belong to the wider democratic movement.

Addressing a programme organised to launch NC leader Dharma Gautam's book - 'BP ra Bidrohaka Ti Din' (BP and Those Days of Revolt), here on Sunday, Thapa observed that BP Koirala's 'Melmilap ko Niti' (policy of national reconciliation) remains highly relevant and continues to draw public discussion.

Thapa highlighted the importance of documenting historical events through credible sources rather than relying on personal recollections. Regarding a recent gathering of the party's establishment faction, Thapa urged the journalists to wait until coming Monday for an official press conference to be organised at the party's central office.

असहमति विशिष्ट वाक्यांश पर केंद्रित छल। डॉ. महत केरऽ मसौदा म॑ ऐतिहासिक आस्था केरऽ पालन करै के स्वतंत्रता के गारंटी के साथ-साथ सनातन परंपरा क॑ राष्ट्रीय पहचान के हिस्सा के रूप म॑ मान्यता दै के वकालत करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । निधि के तर्क छेलै कि पार्टी क॑ अपनऽ पारंपरिक ‘धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता’ केरऽ रुख के सख्ती स॑ पालन करना चाहियऽ, बिना कोनो अतिरिक्त योग्यता के ।

देउबा अंततः हस्तक्षेप केलनि, निर्देश देलनि जे डॉ. महतक मूल मसौदा जेना लिखल गेल अछि तेना पढ़ल जाय। विधानसभा क॑ संबोधित करतें हुअ॑ हुनी कहलकै कि हुनी व्यक्तिगत रूप स॑ हिन्दू के रूप म॑ पहचान करै छै, लेकिन सब व्यक्ति केरऽ अपनऽ-अपनऽ आस्था के पालन करै के स्वतंत्रता के पूरा सम्मान करै छै । पार्टी कार्यकर्ता सब के संबोधित करैत देउवा कहलनि जे, हम व्यक्तिगत रूप स हिन्दू छी। "हम ब्रतबंध पवित्र सूत्र समारोह के पालन केने छी आ हिन्दू परंपरा के अनुसार विवाह केने छी। पशुपतिनाथ के दर्शन करैत प्रार्थना करैत छी।"

धर्म स॑ जुड़लऽ व्यापक राज्य नीति आरू संवैधानिक मुद्दा क॑ संबोधित करतें हुअ॑ हुनी ई बात प॑ जोर देलकै कि अंतिम अधिकार राजनीतिक फरमान के बजाय संप्रभु जनता के पास छै । देउबा न॑ कहलकै कि हालांकि देश म॑ धर्म के मामला म॑ की होय छै या नै होय छै, ई जनता के फैसला प॑ निर्भर करै छै आरू कहलकै कि राष्ट्र म॑ सब लेली धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता होना चाहियऽ ।

दोसर प्रस्ताव के अनुसार विधानसभा निर्णय लेलक जे 15म महाधिवेशन के आयोजन देउबा के नेतृत्व आ निर्देशन में होयत, जाहि में डॉ. शशांक कोइराला के मुख्य संयोजक नियुक्त कयल गेल। गुट देउवा के नेतृत्व में पार्टी के एकजुट करब अधिवेशन के सफलता के लेल बहुत महत्वपूर्ण अछि आ एहि बीच कोइराला देउबा के निर्देशन में नियमित पार्टी के गतिविधि के समन्वय करत।

तेसरऽ प्रस्ताव म॑ संकट के समय म॑ बीपी कोइराला केरऽ १९७६ केरऽ राष्ट्रीय एकता आरू मेलमिलाप केरऽ नीति के हवाला दैत॑ हुअ॑ राष्ट्रवाद आरू लोकतांत्रिक संस्था क॑ मजबूत करै लेली राष्ट्रीय आरू लोकतांत्रिक शक्ति सिनी स॑ बातचीत करै के आग्रह करलऽ गेलऽ छै । चारिम प्रस्ताव वर्तमान संवैधानिक ढाँचा के भीतर संबंधित सरोकारवाला सब स बातचीत के माध्यम स आवश्यक संवैधानिक संशोधन के आगू बढ़ेबाक प्रतिबद्ध अछि।

थापा नेता के विरासत के निजीकरण के खिलाफ चेतावनी |

नेपाली कांग्रेसक अध्यक्ष गगन कुमार थापा बीपी कोइराला आ गणेशमान सिंह सन नेताक विरासत केँ ''निजीकरण'' नहि करबाक चाही वा परिवार धरि सीमित नहि हेबाक चाही, हुनकर राजनीतिक योगदान व्यापक लोकतान्त्रिक आन्दोलनक अछि ताहि पर जोर दैत चेतावनी देलनि ।

नेकपा नेता धर्म गौतम केरऽ पुस्तक - ‘बीपी रा बिद्रोहका ति दिन’ (बीपी आरू विद्रोह केरऽ वू दिन) केरऽ विमोचन लेली आयोजित कार्यक्रम क॑ संबोधित करतें हुअ॑ थापा न॑ देखलकै कि बी.पी.

थापा व्यक्तिगत संस्मरण पर निर्भर रहय के बजाय विश्वसनीय स्रोत के माध्यम सं ऐतिहासिक घटना के दस्तावेजीकरण के महत्व पर प्रकाश देलखिन्ह. हालहि मे पार्टी स्थापना गुटके सभाके संबंधमे थापा पत्रकारसबसँ आग्रह कएलनि जे पार्टीके केन्द्रीय कार्यालयमे आधिकारिक प्रेस कांफ्रेंसके आयोजनामे आबैबला सोमदिन तक प्रतीक्षा करथि ।

title: Nepal's Prisons Overcrowded by 43%, New Facilities Underway - Ratopati
description: Nepal's Prisons Overcrowded by 43%, New Facilities Underway  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. There are 73 prisons across the country. Prisoners convicted by the court and detainees ordered to be held for trial are kept in prisons. According to the data of the Prison Management Department, there are currently 27,798 inmates in prisons across the country.

The government is experimenting with a new system in the jail system to reduce the pressure of inmates by keeping them on parole. Inmates on remand according to court verdicts started being kept on parole from 2081. According to the Criminal Offenses (Sentencing and Implementation) Act-074, inmates can stay outside of detention according to the decision of the parole board.

Despite the implementation of the parole system, the number of inmates in prisons has not decreased. Currently, the data of the Prison Management Department shows that prisons are 43 percent over capacity. The 73 prisons operating across the country have a capacity to accommodate 19,359 inmates, but currently, there are 27,798 inmates in these prisons. The prisons are holding 43 percent more inmates than their capacity.

The second phase of construction of a central-level prison in Khampa Camp, Ward No.-6 of Bidur Municipality, Nuwakot, has been completed to reduce the pressure of inmates from Sundhara (Jagannathdewal), Dillibazar in the Kathmandu Valley, and Nakhhu prison in Lalitpur. The 13 blocks built in Nuwakot can accommodate 1,370 inmates.

On Bhadra 15, 2081, then Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak inaugurated the central prison by transferring 147 inmates from Nuwakot prison to Khampa Camp. The Prison Management Department is gradually sending convicted inmates from the valley there.

Also Read A lot of preparation is required to declare an open prison: Director Chomendra Neupane

Although the concept of open prisons has been debated for a long time, it has not been implemented in practice. The government announces every year that, in accordance with the concept of open prisons, inmates will be linked to employment in small, cottage, and small-scale industries, but this announcement has not been implemented.

Prison Management Department Director Chomendra Neupane stated that the concept of open prisons is being implemented because inmates of productive age are in prison and their labor is being wasted. The Council of Ministers approved the Prison Regulations 2083 this year. Deputy Secretary Neupane informed that the Council of Ministers has further systematized the concept of open prisons by amending the Prison Regulations. He said, 'The regulations have clarified the concept of taking inmates who have served two-thirds of their sentence outside of jail and putting them to work.'

The new regulations include provisions for employing inmates in federal and provincial projects under the concept of open prisons. It was proposed to employ inmates who have been in jail for a long time in national pride projects. However, the proposal to employ inmates and pay them wages has not been implemented.

One-third of the inmates across the country are housed in the 3 prisons within the valley. The capacity of Central Jail Jagannathdewal is only 2300. That jail currently holds 3,986 inmates. The capacity of Dillibazar Prison Office is only 550. The Prison Management Department stated that 629 people are kept there. Nakhhu Prison holds 58 more inmates than its capacity. The capacity of Nakhhu Prison is only 900.

Also Read Central jail inmates generally do not want to go to other jails

Some prisons have more than 400 percent of their capacity in inmates

Some prisons have more than 400 percent of their capacity in inmates. Some, however, do not even have inmates equal to their capacity.

According to the department's data, Taplejung Prison has 484 percent more inmates than its capacity. Similarly, Salyan has 460 percent more inmates than its capacity.

Rukum Paschim Prison has 404 percent more inmates than its capacity. Compared to the prison's capacity, Jumla has 333.33 percent, Gulmi has 328 percent, Udayapur has 268.33 percent, Morang has 282 percent, Ghorahi has 244 percent, Dhankuta has 238 percent, and Saptari has 226 percent more inmates.

Khotehang Prison has a capacity to hold 230 inmates, but only 129 are present. Rasuwa has a capacity to hold 155 inmates, but only 95 are kept there.

Similarly, Kapilvastu Prison, with a capacity of 524 people, holds 411 people, while Naubasta, Banke, with a capacity of 750 people, holds 675 people.

Dolpa Prison, with a capacity to hold 150 inmates, has 18 inmates. Humla Prison, with a capacity to hold 20 inmates, has 13 inmates. Bajhang Prison, with a capacity to hold 101 inmates, has 86 inmates.

A dozen new prisons proposed

Prisons are under construction in 6 districts. Prisons in Panchthar, Jajarkot, Mugu, Humla, Baitadi, and Rasuwa are under construction. It has been proposed to build prisons in a dozen districts.

It has been proposed to build prisons in Jhapa, Dhankuta, Bhojpur, Okhaldhunga, Udayapur, Saptari, Kapilvastu, Lamjung, Pyuthan, Dolakha, Kailali, and Kanchanpur. It has been proposed to start the third phase of construction of the central-level prison in Khampa Camp, Ward No.-6 of Bidur Municipality, Nuwakot. It has also been proposed to start the second phase of construction in Naubasta, informed Director Neupane. The prison under construction in Naubasta, Banke, is of regional level.

A prison is being built in Baitadi with the support of the Sudurpaschim Provincial Government. The prison built by the provincial government in Bajura is in the process of being operational. The provincial government is also building a prison in Jajarkot. The capacity of Kaski Prison Office is also being expanded.

The condition of juvenile reform homes is also not organized and has not truly become reform homes. Incidents of older juveniles beating younger ones and clashes occur repeatedly, making juvenile reform homes turbulent. There are 10 juvenile reform homes in 9 districts across the country. Two juvenile reform homes are in operation in Banke.

Clashes occur frequently in juvenile reform homes when juveniles under 18 and adults are kept together. Spokesperson (Joint Secretary) of the Ministry of Women, Children, Senior Citizens, and Social Security, Chakra Bahadur Buda, told Ratopati that a law is in the process of being drafted to separate minors and adults.

He said, 'It has been proposed to send juveniles over 18 years of age and those with bad conduct from juvenile reform homes to prisons.'

The draft bill, approved by the Council of Ministers, has been registered in the Parliament Secretariat. Joint Secretary Buda stated that the bill proposes to send juveniles who committed crimes as minors and stayed in reform homes to prison once they become adults.

The management of juvenile reform homes has been handled by the Ministry of Women, Children, Senior Citizens, and Social Security since August 2082. There are currently 1200 juveniles in juvenile reform homes across the country. Juveniles over 18 years of age are kept in the central prison in Nuwakot and Naubasta.

किछ जेल मे कैदी के क्षमता के 400 प्रतिशत सं बेसि अछि. मुदा किछु गोटे के क्षमता के बराबर कैदी तक नहिं छनि.

विभाग केरऽ आंकड़ऽ के अनुसार ताप्लेजुंग जेल म॑ ओकरऽ क्षमता स॑ ४८४ प्रतिशत अधिक कैदी छै । तहिना सलयन मे सेहो अपन क्षमता स 460 प्रतिशत बेसी कैदी अछि।

रुकुम पश्चिम जेल मे ओकर क्षमता स 404 प्रतिशत बेसी कैदी अछि। जेल के क्षमता के तुलना में जुमला में 333.33 प्रतिशत, गुल्मी में 328 प्रतिशत, उदयपुर में 268.33 प्रतिशत, मोरंग में 282 प्रतिशत, घोराही में 244 प्रतिशत, धनकुटा में 238 प्रतिशत, आ सप्तरी में 226 प्रतिशत बेसी कैदी अछि।

खोटेहांग जेल मे 230 कैदी कए रखबाक क्षमता अछि, मुदा मात्र 129 कैदी मौजूद अछि। रसुवा मे 155 कैदी कए रखबाक क्षमता अछि, मुदा ओतय मात्र 95 कैदी कए राखल गेल अछि।

तहिना 524 लोकक क्षमता वाला कपिलवस्तु कारागार मे 411 लोक बैसल अछि, जखन कि नौबस्ता, बांके मे 750 लोकक क्षमता वाला 675 लोकक बैसबाक व्यवस्था अछि।

150 कैदी रखबाक क्षमता वाला डोल्पा जेल मे 18 कैदी अछि। 20 कैदी रखबाक क्षमता वाला हुमला जेल मे 13 कैदी अछि। 101 कैदी रखबाक क्षमता वाला बझांग जेल मे 86 कैदी अछि।

एक दर्जन नव जेल प्रस्तावित

6 जिला मे जेल क निर्माण भ रहल अछि। पंचथर, जाजरकोट, मुगु, हुमला, बैतडी, आ रसुवा के जेल निर्माणाधीन अछि। एक दर्जन जिला मे जेल बनेबाक प्रस्ताव आयल अछि।

झापा, धनकुटा, भोजपुर, ओखलढुंगा, उदयपुर, सप्तरी, कपिलवस्तु, लमजुंग, प्यूठान, दोलखा, कैलाली, आ कंचनपुर मे जेल बनेबाक प्रस्ताव राखल गेल अछि । नुवाकोट के बिदुर नगरपालिका वार्ड नम्बर ६ खम्पा कैम्प मे केन्द्रीय स्तरीय कारागार के तेसर चरण के निर्माण शुरु करबाक प्रस्ताव राखल गेल अछि । नौबस्ता मे दोसर चरण क निर्माण शुरू करबाक प्रस्ताव सेहो राखल गेल अछि, निदेशक न्यूपाने जानकारी देलथि। बांके के नौबस्ता में निर्माणाधीन जेल क्षेत्रीय स्तर के अछि।

सुदुरपस्चिम प्रान्तीय सरकारके सहयोगमे बैतडीमे जेल बनाओल जा रहल अछि । बाजुरा मे प्रांतीय सरकार द्वारा निर्मित जेल परिचालन मे लागल अछि। प्रांतीय सरकार जाजरकोट मे जेल सेहो बना रहल अछि। कास्की जेल कार्यालय के क्षमता के सेहो विस्तार कएल जा रहल अछि.

किशोर सुधार गृह केरऽ हालत भी संगठित नै छै आरू सही मायने म॑ सुधार घर नै बनी गेलऽ छै । पैघ किशोर कें छोट बच्चाक कें पीटय कें घटना आ झड़प बेर-बेर होयत छै, जेकरा सं किशोर सुधार घर उथल-पुथल भ जायत छै. देश भर मे 9 जिला मे 10 किशोर सुधार घर अछि। बांके मे दूटा किशोर सुधार घर संचालित अछि।

किशोर सुधार घरक मे अक्सर झड़प होयत छै जखन 18 साल सं कम उम्र कें किशोर आ वयस्कक कें एक संगे राखल जायत छै. महिला, बाल, वरिष्ठ नागरिक, आ सामाजिक सुरक्षा मन्त्रालयके प्रवक्ता (संयुक्त सचिव) चक्रबहादुर बुडा राटोपतिके बतौलनि जे नाबालिग आ वयस्कके अलग करबाक लेल कानून बनेबाक प्रक्रिया चलि रहल अछि ।

ओ कहला जे 18 साल स बेसी उम्र क किशोर आ खराब आचरण वाला कए किशोर सुधार घर स जेल मे पठेबाक प्रस्ताव अछि।'

मन्त्री परिषद्द्वारा अनुमोदित विधेयकके मसौदा संसद सचिवालयमे दर्ज कराओल गेल अछि । संयुक्त सचिव बुडा के कहनाय छनि जे एहि विधेयक मे नाबालिग के रूप मे अपराध करय वाला आओर रिफॉर्म होम मे रहय वाला किशोर के वयस्क भ गेला पर जेल भेजय के प्रस्ताव अछि.

किशोर सुधार घरक कें प्रबंधन अगस्त 2082 सं महिला, बाल, वरिष्ठ नागरिक, आ सामाजिक सुरक्षा मंत्रालय द्वारा संचालित कैल जायत छै.अखन देश भर मे किशोर सुधार घरक मे 1200 किशोर छै. 18 साल सं बेसि उम्र के किशोर के नुवाकोट आओर नौबास्ता के केंद्रीय जेल मे राखल गेल अछि.

title: Nepal Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association and Ministry Reach Agreement, Protests Halted - Ratopati
description: Nepal Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association and Ministry Reach Agreement, Protests Halted  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. An agreement has been reached between the protesting Nepal Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association and the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Security on Monday. Following discussions between the Minister, Secretary, President, Advisor, and officials of the Nepal Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association, an agreement was reached to postpone the protest.

The association had been conducting attention-grabbing programs with 15-point demands since Shrawan 22 and had decided to stop sending workers to destination countries from Bhadra 1. In today's discussion, it was informed that most of the issues raised by the association in its 15-point demands are policy-related and are being included in the process of amending the Foreign Employment Act and Regulations.

An agreement has been reached for the Ministry and the Association to make maximum efforts to conclude the amendment process in a way that makes the field of foreign employment transparent, safe, and dignified as soon as possible. Regarding the overall demands, if the entrepreneurs request their issues to the Department of Foreign Employment with additional evidence and documents as per the law, the department will provide necessary administrative facilitation. If a solution is not found there, the discussion has concluded with the provision that they can appeal to the Ministry formally.

Based on the agreement, the Nepal Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs Association has committed to ending all pressure programs conducted from the date of Bhadra 1 itself, as mentioned in the press release issued by the Ministry of Labour's Joint Secretary and Spokesperson Pitambar Ghimire.

title: Deuba’s Return: Nepal’s Test of Democratic Renewal - Khabarhub
description: Deuba’s Return: Nepal’s Test of Democratic Renewal  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
Sher Bahadur Deuba’s return to Nepal on 13 August 2026 is more than the return of a former five-time prime minister and veteran leader of the Nepali Congress (NC). It is a moment that brings together three larger questions about Nepal’s democratic future. Can accountability remain above political retaliation?

Can the Nepali Congress overcome its internal factionalism and generational divide? And can Nepal’s traditional democratic establishment adapt to a political landscape fundamentally transformed by the upheavals of 2025 and the electoral mandate of 2026? These questions are interconnected.

Deuba has returned at a very different historical moment from the one in which he built his political career. Nepal has experienced a profound political rupture. The September 2025 Gen-Z uprising challenged the legitimacy and credibility of the established political class. The March 2026 election then translated that public frustration into an electoral mandate for a new generation of political leadership.

The rise of Balendra Shah and the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) was therefore not simply an electoral change. It represented a deeper public demand for accountability, competence, generational renewal and a different relationship between citizens and the state.

Deuba’s return has to be understood against that backdrop.

A Return in a Different Historical Moment

Upon returning, Deuba invoked national unity and the tradition of B.P. Koirala’s 1976 return to Nepal and his call for national reconciliation. The historical reference is significant, but the circumstances are fundamentally different. B.P. Koirala returned to confront an authoritarian political order. Deuba returns to a constitutional democratic system in which the electorate has already expressed its dissatisfaction with the established political class through an extraordinary political transition.

The 2026 election was, in significant measure, a rejection of established political practices. That message cannot be ignored.

The challenge today is therefore not simply to restore democracy. It is to renew it. That distinction matters. Deuba’s appeal for unity among nationalist and democratic forces can be interpreted in two ways. It can become an attempt by an established political generation to recover lost political space. Or it can become a bridge between institutional experience and a new generation seeking political renewal. The difference will depend on what follows the rhetoric.

The Nepali Congress Test

Deuba’s return also comes at a critical moment for the NC. The party remains divided by competing leadership claims and organizational factions. The dispute between the Deuba camp and the leadership associated with Gagan Thapa raises a larger question than who controls the party.

It raises the question of whether the Nepali Congress can reinvent itself. There are several possibilities. The first is limited reconciliation: competing factions agree on a practical accommodation, preserve party unity and gradually facilitate a generational transition.

The second is prolonged fragmentation: factional competition continues, organizational structures become increasingly divided, and the party loses further political relevance.

The third is deeper democratic renewal: the party uses the current crisis to reform its organization, strengthen internal democracy, embrace generational change and redefine its role as a modern democratic opposition.

The third would be the most constructive outcome, not merely for the NC, but for Nepal’s democratic system.

A democracy requires more than a strong government.

It also requires a credible opposition capable of scrutinizing power, offering alternatives and defending institutions without seeking to restore an older political order.

The Legal Test: Accountability Without Retaliation

The most sensitive dimension of Deuba’s return is the ongoing money-laundering investigation.

This must remain a legal matter, not become another front in Nepal’s political contestation. Deuba has denied the allegations and has consistently argued that his property declarations were properly submitted. His legal strategy has included challenging the earlier arrest process, asserting procedural and jurisdictional deficiencies, demonstrating a willingness to cooperate with investigators and returning to Nepal after medical treatment abroad.

The Supreme Court’s intervention concerning the earlier arrest warrant was an important reminder that even politically significant investigations must comply with law and procedure. The underlying investigation, however, remains a separate matter. The critical principle is simple: Procedural protection does not establish innocence, just as investigation does not establish guilt.

Evidence must determine the outcome.

For the Shah government, this creates a difficult political and institutional balance. If the government retreats from the investigation because Deuba is a senior political figure, it risks accusations of selective justice.

If it pursues the case aggressively in ways that appear politically motivated or procedurally weak, it risks strengthening Deuba’s argument that the process is retaliatory.

The strongest position for the government is therefore neither political leniency nor political confrontation. It is institutional distance.

The government must therefore demonstrate that accountability applies equally to friends and opponents. It must allow independent institutions to function.

Investigate on the basis of evidence. Prosecute where the evidence meets the legal threshold. Respect judicial decisions. Provide due process. And allow the courts to determine guilt or innocence. A government committed to ending impunity must demonstrate that accountability is stronger than politics. That is ultimately the best protection against the charge of political revenge.

The Larger Political Reality

Deuba’s return also illustrates a larger contradiction in contemporary Nepal. The country still needs the institutional memory of the political generation that built and defended multiparty democracy. But the electorate has also made clear that it does not want a simple return to the politics of the past.

The 2026 election was, in significant measure, a rejection of established political practices. That message cannot be ignored. Traditional parties cannot rebuild their relevance simply by criticizing the new government, invoking their historical contribution or forming defensive alliances against a new political force.

They must answer a much harder question: Why should a younger generation believe that the old political parties have genuinely changed?

The answer will have to come through action. Organizational reform. Generational transition. Internal democracy. Credible economic policies. Institutional accountability. And a new relationship between political parties and citizens.

The political transformation of 2025–26 has changed the baseline. The old political establishment cannot assume that historical legitimacy alone will translate into contemporary political legitimacy.

Beyond Deuba: Three Possible Futures

Deuba’s return could therefore lead Nepal toward several different political trajectories. One, managed reconciliation. The competing factions of the NC reach an accommodation. Deuba assumes an elder-statesman role while younger leaders increasingly take responsibility for the party’s future.

This could preserve institutional continuity while allowing generational transition.

Second, prolonged fragmentation. Factional disputes continue, possibly producing parallel structures or a formal organizational rupture. Such fragmentation would weaken the traditional democratic opposition and could allow the RSP to consolidate its political dominance.

Sher Bahadur Deuba’s return should therefore not be viewed simply as the comeback of a veteran politician. It is a test of Nepal’s ability to manage political transition. It tests whether accountability can be pursued without retaliation.

Finally, democratic realignment. The more consequential possibility is that the traditional political parties recognize that the political environment has fundamentally changed. Rather than attempting to restore the old order, they could compete to build a new democratic order, one based on competence, transparency, institutional integrity, economic delivery and generational leadership.

That would transform the current political crisis into an opportunity for democratic renewal.

The Government Has a Test Too

The responsibility does not rest with Deuba or the NC alone. The Shah government is also being tested. Its mandate is based heavily on accountability and political transformation. But political transformation becomes sustainable only when institutions become stronger than personalities.

The government must therefore demonstrate that accountability applies equally to friends and opponents. It must allow independent institutions to function. It must respect judicial processes even when decisions are inconvenient. And it must distinguish between legitimate political opposition and obstruction of reform. The temptation in a period of political transition is to treat the previous establishment as an obstacle to be permanently dismantled. That would be a mistake.

A mature democracy does not eliminate its political opponents.

It institutionalizes competition. The new government therefore has an opportunity to demonstrate that Nepal’s political transformation is not merely a change of political actors but a transition toward stronger institutions.

Experience and Renewal Are Not Opposites

There is also a broader lesson in Deuba’s return. Nepal should not confuse generational renewal with the rejection of experience. Nor should it confuse political experience with a permanent entitlement to political leadership. The two must be reconciled. Veteran leaders possess institutional memory, historical perspective and an understanding of Nepal’s complex political evolution. Younger leaders bring different expectations, new technologies, different approaches to governance and a stronger demand for accountability.

Nepal does not need the old political order restored. Nor does it need the old political establishment permanently excluded. Nepal needs a democratic system capable of renewal.

The challenge is to connect the two. Deuba’s most significant contribution at this stage may therefore not be another political comeback. It may be to facilitate a responsible transition between generations. That would be a different kind of political legacy.

Conclusion: From Political Replacement to Democratic Renewal

Sher Bahadur Deuba’s return should therefore not be viewed simply as the comeback of a veteran politician. It is a test of Nepal’s ability to manage political transition. It tests whether accountability can be pursued without retaliation.

It tests whether opposition politics can remain constructive without becoming an attempt to restore the past. It tests whether the NC can transform experience into renewal. And it tests whether the new government can convert its electoral mandate into institutional change rather than merely political dominance.

The behavior of major states and political leaders is increasingly characterized by aggressive self-interest. This tension is best understood through the philosophical lenses of Niccolò Machiavelli and Immanuel Kant. The Machiavellian framework views politics as an uncompromising, zero-sum struggle for survival and dominance, where the ends justify the means and moral considerations are secondary to power.

Conversely, the Kantian framework champions a universal moral duty, international law, and the “categorical imperative”, the principle that actors must behave according to rules they would want universally applied, treating others as ends in themselves rather than as disposable tools.

Today, this philosophical friction is playing out not only on the grand stage of global great-power competition but also within the internal political fabric of developing nations like Nepal.

Nepal does not need the old political order restored. Nor does it need the old political establishment permanently excluded. Nepal needs a democratic system capable of renewal. The significance of Deuba’s return will ultimately depend not on how many supporters welcome him, how many factions rally around him, or how forcefully he re-enters political debate.

It will depend on whether his generation can help create space for the next one. The central question, therefore, is not whether Sher Bahadur Deuba can return to politics. The larger question is whether Nepal’s democratic establishment can renew itself without becoming captive to its past.

That is the real test of democratic renewal in post-2026 Nepal.

अतः सरकार क॑ ई प्रदर्शित करना चाहियऽ कि जवाबदेही दोस्त आरू विरोधी प॑ समान रूप स॑ लागू होय छै । एकरा स्वतंत्र संस्था कए काज करबाक अनुमति देबाक चाही।

बड़का राजनीतिक यथार्थ

देउबा के वापसी समकालीन नेपाल में एकटा पैघ विरोधाभास के सेहो दर्शाबैत अछि | देश क॑ अखनी भी वू राजनीतिक पीढ़ी केरऽ संस्थागत स्मृति के जरूरत छै जे बहुदलीय लोकतंत्र के निर्माण आरू रक्षा करलकै । मुदा मतदाता इहो साफ क देलक अछि जे ओ पहिने के राजनीति मे साधारण वापसी नहि चाहैत अछि.

२०२६ केरऽ चुनाव, महत्वपूर्ण मात्रा म॑, स्थापित राजनीतिक प्रथा केरऽ अस्वीकार छेलै । ओहि संदेश केँ नजरअंदाज नहि कयल जा सकैत अछि। पारंपरिक दल खाली नयका सरकार के आलोचना करी क॑, अपनऽ ऐतिहासिक योगदान के आह्वान करी क॑ या नया राजनीतिक शक्ति के खिलाफ रक्षात्मक गठबंधन करी क॑ अपनऽ प्रासंगिकता के पुनर्निर्माण नै करी सकै छै ।

एकर जवाब कर्म के माध्यम स आबय पड़त। संगठनात्मक सुधार। पीढ़ीगत संक्रमण। आन्तरिक लोकतंत्र। विश्वसनीय आर्थिक नीतियाँ। संस्थागत जवाबदेही। आ राजनीतिक दल आ नागरिकक बीच नव संबंध।

देउबा सँ परे : तीन संभावित भविष्य

एहि लेल देउबा के वापसी नेपाल के कई अलग-अलग राजनीतिक प्रक्षेपवक्र दिस ल जा सकैत अछि. एक, प्रबंधित सुलह। नेकां के प्रतिस्पर्धी गुट एकटा आवास तक पहुंचैत अछि। देउबा बड़का-राजनेता के भूमिका ग्रहण करैत छथि जखन कि छोटका नेता पार्टी के भविष्य के जिम्मेदारी तेजी सं लैत छथिन्ह.

एहि लेल शेर बहादुर देउबा के वापसी के सिर्फ एकटा अनुभवी राजनीतिज्ञ के वापसी के रूप मे नहि देखल जेबाक चाही. ई नेपाल के राजनीतिक संक्रमण के प्रबंधन के क्षमता के परीक्षा छै. ई परीक्षण करै छै कि बिना प्रतिशोध के जवाबदेही के पीछा करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै कि नै ।

अंत मे लोकतांत्रिक पुनर्गठन। अधिक परिणामी संभावना ई छै कि पारंपरिक राजनीतिक दल ई बात क॑ स्वीकार करै छै कि राजनीतिक माहौल म॑ मौलिक रूप स॑ बदलाव आबी गेलऽ छै । पुरान व्यवस्था क॑ बहाल करै के कोशिश करै के बजाय वू एगो नया लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था के निर्माण लेली प्रतिस्पर्धा करी सकै छै, जे दक्षता, पारदर्शिता, संस्थागत अखंडता, आर्थिक वितरण आरू पीढ़ी के नेतृत्व प॑ आधारित होय ।

जे वर्तमान राजनीतिक संकट कए लोकतांत्रिक नवीकरण क अवसर मे बदलि देत।

सरकार के सेहो टेस्ट अछि

जिम्मेवारी असगरे देउबा वा नेकपा पर नहि अछि। शाह सरकार के सेहो परीक्षण भ रहल अछि. एकरऽ जनादेश बहुत हद तक जवाबदेही आरू राजनीतिक परिवर्तन प॑ आधारित छै । मुदा राजनीतिक परिवर्तन तखने स्थायित्व होइत अछि जखन संस्था व्यक्तित्व सँ बेसी मजबूत भ' जाइत अछि ।

अतः सरकार क॑ ई प्रदर्शित करना चाहियऽ कि जवाबदेही दोस्त आरू विरोधी प॑ समान रूप स॑ लागू होय छै । एकरा स्वतंत्र संस्था कए काज करबाक अनुमति देबाक चाही। ओकरा न्यायिक प्रक्रियाक सम्मान करबाक चाही तखनो जखन निर्णय असुविधाजनक हो । आरू ओकरा जायज राजनीतिक विरोध आरू सुधार म॑ बाधा पहुँचै के बीच भेद करना चाहियऽ । राजनीतिक संक्रमण के दौर में प्रलोभन ई छै कि पिछला संस्थापन के स्थायी रूप स भंग करय के बाधा के रूप में देखल जाय। जे गलती होयत।

परिपक्व लोकतंत्र अपन राजनीतिक विरोधी के समाप्त नहि करैत अछि ।

ई प्रतिस्पर्धा के संस्थागत बनाबै छै। अतः नव सरकार के ई देखाबै के मौका छै कि नेपाल के राजनीतिक परिवर्तन खाली राजनीतिक अभिनेता के परिवर्तन नै बल्कि मजबूत संस्था के तरफ संक्रमण छै ।

अनुभव आ नवीकरण विपरीत नहि होइत छैक

देउबा’क वापसी मे एकटा व्यापक पाठ सेहो अछि. नेपाल के पीढ़ी के नवीकरण के अनुभव के अस्वीकार स भ्रमित नै करबाक चाही। आ नै राजनीतिक अनुभव के राजनीतिक नेतृत्व के स्थायी हक स भ्रमित करबाक चाही। दुनूक बीच मेल-मिलाप हेबाक चाही। दिग्गज नेता सब के पास संस्थागत स्मृति, ऐतिहासिक परिप्रेक्ष्य आ नेपाल के जटिल राजनीतिक विकास के समझ छैन्ह । युवा नेता अलग-अलग अपेक्षा, नया तकनीक, शासन के अलग-अलग दृष्टिकोण आरू जवाबदेही के मजबूत मांग लानै छै.

नेपाल के पुरान राजनीतिक व्यवस्था के बहाल करय के जरूरत नहिं. आ ने पुरान राजनीतिक प्रतिष्ठान के स्थायी रूप स बहिष्कृत करबाक आवश्यकता अछि। नेपाल के नवीकरण में सक्षम लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था चाही।

चुनौती अछि जे दुनू कए जोड़ल जाए। एहि स्तर पर देउबा के सबस महत्वपूर्ण योगदान एहि लेल एकटा आओर राजनीतिक वापसी नहि भ सकैत अछि. ई पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी के बीच जिम्मेदार संक्रमण के सुविधा देबय लेल भ सकैत अछि. जे एकटा अलग तरहक राजनीतिक विरासत होयत।

निष्कर्ष : राजनीतिक प्रतिस्थापन स लोकतांत्रिक नवीकरण तक

एहि लेल शेर बहादुर देउबा के वापसी के सिर्फ एकटा अनुभवी राजनीतिज्ञ के वापसी के रूप मे नहि देखल जेबाक चाही. ई नेपाल के राजनीतिक संक्रमण के प्रबंधन के क्षमता के परीक्षा छै. ई परीक्षण करै छै कि बिना प्रतिशोध के जवाबदेही के पीछा करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै कि नै ।

ई परीक्षण करै छै कि विपक्षी राजनीति अतीत क॑ बहाल करै के कोशिश नै बनी क॑ रचनात्मक बनी सकै छै कि नै । एहि मे इ परीक्षण कैल गेल अछि जे की नेकां अनुभव कए नवीकरण मे बदलि सकैत अछि। आरू ई परीक्षण करै छै कि की नया सरकार अपनऽ चुनावी जनादेश क॑ खाली राजनीतिक वर्चस्व के बजाय संस्थागत परिवर्तन म॑ बदली सकै छै ।

प्रमुख राज्य आरू राजनीतिक नेता केरऽ व्यवहार म॑ आक्रामक स्वार्थ केरऽ विशेषता बढ़ी रहलऽ छै । ई तनाव क॑ निकोलो मैकियावेली आरू इमैनुएल कांट केरऽ दार्शनिक चश्मा स॑ सबसें अच्छा समझलऽ जाय छै । मैकियावेली ढाँचा राजनीति क॑ अस्तित्व आरू वर्चस्व लेली एगो बेमेल, शून्य-योग संघर्ष के रूप म॑ देखै छै, जहाँ अंत साधन क॑ जायज ठहराबै छै आरू नैतिक विचार सत्ता के प्रति गौण छै ।

एकरऽ विपरीत, कांटियन ढाँचा एक सार्वभौमिक नैतिक कर्तव्य, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय कानून, आरू “श्रेणीबद्ध अनिवार्य” के समर्थन करै छै, ई सिद्धांत कि अभिनेता सिनी क॑ वू नियमऽ के अनुसार व्यवहार करना चाहियऽ जेकरा वू सार्वभौमिक रूप स॑ लागू करना चाहै छै, दोसरऽ क॑ डिस्पोजेबल औजार के रूप म॑ नै बल्कि खुद म॑ अंत के रूप म॑ मान॑ छै ।

आइ ई दार्शनिक घर्षण वैश्विक महाशक्ति प्रतिस्पर्धाक भव्य मंच पर नहि अपितु नेपाल सन विकासशील राष्ट्रक आन्तरिक राजनीतिक ताना-बाना मे सेहो खेलाइत अछि ।

नेपाल के पुरान राजनीतिक व्यवस्था के बहाल करय के जरूरत नहिं. आ ने पुरान राजनीतिक प्रतिष्ठान के स्थायी रूप स बहिष्कृत करबाक आवश्यकता अछि। नेपाल के नवीकरण में सक्षम लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था चाही। देउबा के वापसी के महत्व अंततः एहि बात पर निर्भर करत जे कतेक समर्थक हुनकर स्वागत करैत छथि, कतेक गुट हुनका चारू कात जुटताह, आ ने कतेक जबरदस्ती राजनीतिक बहस मे फेर सं प्रवेश करताह.

ई एहि बात पर निर्भर करत जे हुनकर पीढ़ी अगिला के लेल जगह बनेबा मे मदद क सकैत अछि कि नहि. अतः केंद्रीय सवाल ई नै छै कि शेरबहादुर देउबा राजनीति में वापस आबी सकै छै कि नै । एहि स पैघ सवाल इ अछि जे की नेपाल क लोकतांत्रिक प्रतिष्ठान अपन अतीत क बंदी नहि बनल अपना कए नवीनीकरण क सकैत अछि।

२०२६ के बाद के नेपाल में लोकतान्त्रिक नवीकरण के असली परीक्षा यही छै ।

full_article:
The main streets of Kathmandu were surprisingly clear on the late April morning as we made our way to the office of the Minister of Urban Development in response to his urgent call.

Only a few days after the massive earthquake that had rocked Nepal in 2015, the debris of broken walls and fallen electricity lines littered the roadside, but most buildings were still intact.

A small aftershock, undetectable from the car, brought people hastening out of their homes, the fear and uncertainty of the past catastrophic days etched onto their faces. With me was a New Zealand government official who had just arrived from Wellington to join the consular team which had gathered from the High Commission in New Delhi and beyond to support the crisis response.

Minister Narayan Khadka, flushed from the stress of his role, rose from his chair as we were ushered into the Singha Darbar office, his desk backed by a limp Nepali flag. The Minister had missed the earthquake, having just returned from representing Nepal at the ANZAC centenary at Gallipoli in Turkey on the same day. (He was outraged that Prince Charles had allegedly forgotten to recognise the Gurkha sacrifice on that ill-fated peninsula, and I had trouble getting him back on topic).

“You need New Zealanders to help your Nepali engineers?” I prompted him. “Yes of course,” the Minister was impatient. “So many Nepalis were trained by your Kiwi guys, and they tell me that Richard Sharpe wrote our earthquake building code guidelines more than 20 years ago. We need to request your urgent help with earthquake expertise to support our Nepali seismic specialists to assess the structural safety of our buildings, both public and private. Our engineers need a team of experts from New Zealand, preferably including Richard, to come here as soon as possible.”

New Zealand’s location on the rim of the Pacific Ring of Fire ensures that the country is expert on earthquakes, constant seismic activity, mitigation techniques and geodetic disruption. Minister Khadka was referring to an influential UNDP project in the early 1990s led by Richard Sharpe that resulted in the creation of Nepal’s building code guidelines, educational exchanges with New Zealand universities, and eventually the formation of Kathmandu’s highly regarded core institution, the National Society for Earthquake Technology Nepal (NSET).

In Nepal, earthquake expertise today is rooted in the experience gained by this game-changing project. In much the same way that Edmund Hillary and Everest forever link Nepal and New Zealand, it is less well-known that earthquakes are another powerful strand of the relationship. This reputation rests firmly on the shoulders of one man, Richard Sharpe.

The gathering of Richard Sharpe's former colleagues and admirers included engineers from government, academia and consultants in Kathmandu in May 2026. Photo: LISA CHOEGYAL

After some preparatory visits, in 1991 Richard settled into an office in Baber Mahal next to the Director General of Buildings. His not inconsiderable task was seismic hazard mapping and risk assessment in order to prepare and implement a National Building Code.

He writes: ‘We provided much more than just the design-for-earthquake aspects. The development of alternative building materials and technologies included an inventory of 55 typical houses throughout Nepal.'

Richard’s team of Nepali specialists set to work on the building code, tailored to Nepal’s specific conditions. Most homes were self-built or locally constructed without masons or engineers, so the code included mandatory rules-of-thumb for common building types and detailed guidelines for less formal structures.

The first training workshop was held in Dharan in 1993 for government inspectors. Photos: RICHARD SHARPE

The code also had to have relevance for professionally designed modern buildings and new high rises. It soon became apparent that the bulk of government officials and inspectors lacked the capacity to effectively implement its recommendations, so the team went back to basics.

The first training program was held in Dharan in 1993. Amod Dixit, one of his team who went on to establish NSET, explained that a cultural sea-change was required in both government and local thought processes.

He said, “What was so inspirational about Richard Sharpe was that he encouraged us to work out the Nepal-specific solutions for ourselves, never dictating them to us. Under his leadership we grew in confidence, but without his insights and experience we would never have got there.”

MANTRA

Richard Sharpe’s mantra was the opposite to donor dependency and recognised his colleagues’ skill. “You Nepali engineers can do it yourself, and we will support and guide you,” he used to say.

In the final weeks of the building code project, Richard worked with the Nepal team to form a learned society to maintain the momentum, and they did. Funding was found and NSET was born, its statute based on that of the New Zealand Society for Earthquake Engineering.

In 2010, I was amongst the audience who attended a major conference with international earthquake specialists brought together by NSET and the United Nations beneath the chandeliers of the Yak & Yeti Hotel in Kathmandu. The Kiwi television personality Bob Parker, now Mayor of Christchurch, was invited as keynote speaker.

Dramatically retelling the city’s story of how they survived a recent Magnitude 7.1 earthquake with zero fatalities, the charismatic Mayor Bob electrified the gathering by banging his lectern for the 40 seconds of its duration. It seemed like forever. Not long after he returned home, Christchurch was not so lucky. A second major shock killed 185 people on 22 February 2011, devastating the city.

Richard Sharpe led the Kiwi structural engineering team which responded in 2015 to the Minister’s request. He was back in Kathmandu in May to speak at a seminar with support from the Asia New Zealand Foundation. I met him at a lunch hosted by his acolytes, engineers from government, academia and consultancy spheres, now distinguished grey old men who had shaped Nepal and who continue to hold him in the highest esteem.

In an elegant navy jacket, Richard blushed his way through the laudatory speeches as we helped ourselves to the buffet. Despite his embarrassment at the accolades, Richard’s passion and knowledge were irrepressible as we discussed various funding opportunities for NSET to retrofit and base isolate remote hospitals, schools and other public buildings such as the Supreme Court and Singha Darbar to withstand future hazards. NSET has recently been sharing its expertise in Bhutan and beyond.

“There is a very interesting situation right now whereby India has withdrawn the recent revision of its earthquake code because of a public outcry over perceived costs,” he said. “This update proposed to use the same techniques and approaches that Nepal adopted over thirty years ago in our project to set the design forces and seismic zoning. You could say that India is catching up to Nepal.”

अप्रैल के अंतिम दिन भोर में काठमांडू के मुख्य सड़क आश्चर्यजनक रूप स साफ छल, जखन कि हम सब हुनकर तत्काल आह्वान के प्रतिक्रिया में नगर विकास मंत्री के कार्यालय दिस बढ़लहुं।

2015 मे नेपाल मे आयल भारी भूकंप के मात्र किछुए दिन बाद टूटल देबाल आ खसल बिजली लाइन के मलबा सड़क के कात मे कूड़ा-करकट भ गेल छल, मुदा अधिकांश भवन एखनो बरकरार छल।

गाड़ी सं पता नै चलय वाला एकटा छोट सन आफ्टरशॉक लोक के जल्दी-जल्दी घर सं बाहर निकालि देलक, बीतल विनाशकारी दिनक डर आ अनिश्चितता ओकर चेहरा पर खोदल गेल. हमरा संग न्यूजीलैंड केरऽ एगो सरकारी अधिकारी छेलै जे अभी-अभी वेलिंगटन स॑ वू कांसुलर टीम म॑ शामिल होय लेली ऐलऽ छेलै जे संकट केरऽ प्रतिक्रिया के समर्थन लेली नई दिल्ली आरू ओकरा स॑ बाहर केरऽ हाई कमीशन स॑ जमा होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

अपन भूमिकाक तनावसँ लाल भऽ गेल मंत्री नारायण खड्का हमरा सभकेँ सिंघा दरबार कार्यालयमे प्रवेश करैत कुर्सीसँ उठलाह, हुनकर डेस्क पर लंगड़ा नेपाली झंडाक समर्थन छल । मंत्री भूकंप स चूकि गेल छलाह, ओ एखनहि ओही दिन तुर्की के गैलीपोली मे एनजाक शताब्दी समारोह मे नेपाल के प्रतिनिधित्व क वापस आयल छलाह. (ओकरा ई बात आक्रोश छल जे राजकुमार चार्ल्स कथित तौर पर ओहि दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण प्रायद्वीप पर गोर्खा बलिदान केँ चिन्हब बिसरि गेल छलाह, आ हमरा हुनका विषय पर वापस अनबा मे परेशानी भेल)।

“अहाँकेँ अपन नेपाली इंजीनियर सभक मददि करबाक लेल न्यूजीलैंडक लोक चाही?” हम हुनका प्रेरित केलियनि। “हँ अवश्य” मंत्री अधीर भ’ गेलाह। "एतेक नेपाली के अहाँक कीवी लड़का सब प्रशिक्षित केने छल, आ ओ सब हमरा कहैत अछि जे रिचर्ड शार्प 20 साल स बेसी पहिने हमर भूकंप बिल्डिंग कोड के गाइडलाइन लिखने छलाह। हमरा सब के भूकंप विशेषज्ञता के संग अहां सब स तत्काल मदद के आग्रह करय के जरूरत अछि जे हमर नेपाली भूकंपीय विशेषज्ञ सब के सहयोग करी जे हमर भवन के संरचनात्मक सुरक्षा के आकलन करी, सार्वजनिक आ निजी दुनु। हमर इंजीनियर सब के एतय आबय लेल न्यूजीलैंड के विशेषज्ञ के टीम के जरूरत अछि, बेसी नीक रहत जे रिचर्ड सहित जल्द सँ जल्द।”

न्यूजीलैंड केरऽ प्रशांत रिंग ऑफ फायर केरऽ रिम प॑ स्थित होय के कारण ई सुनिश्चित होय छै कि देश भूकंप, लगातार भूकंपीय गतिविधि, शमन तकनीक आरू भूगणितीय व्यवधान के विशेषज्ञ छै । मंत्री खड्का न॑ १९९० केरऽ दशक केरऽ शुरुआत म॑ रिचर्ड शार्प केरऽ नेतृत्व म॑ यूएनडीपी केरऽ एगो प्रभावशाली परियोजना के तरफ इशारा करी रहलऽ छेलै जेकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप नेपाल केरऽ बिल्डिंग कोड गाइडलाइन के निर्माण, न्यूजीलैंड केरऽ विश्वविद्यालयऽ के साथ शैक्षिक आदान-प्रदान, आरू अंततः काठमांडू केरऽ उच्च सम्मानित कोर संस्था नेशनल सोसाइटी फॉर भूकंप टेक्नोलॉजी नेपाल (एनएसईटी) केरऽ गठन करलऽ गेलै ।

नेपाल मे आइ भूकम्प विशेषज्ञता एहि खेल बदलय वाला परियोजना स प्राप्त अनुभव मे जड़ि जमा लेने अछि । जेना एडमंड हिलेरी आरू एवरेस्ट हमेशा लेली नेपाल आरू न्यूजीलैंड क॑ जोड़ै छै, वू तरह स॑ ई बात कम जानलऽ जाय छै कि भूकंप ई संबंध केरऽ एगो आरू शक्तिशाली तार छै । ई प्रतिष्ठा एकटा आदमी रिचर्ड शार्प के कान्ह पर मजबूती स टिकल अछि ।

रिचर्ड शार्प केरऽ पूर्व सहयोगी आरू प्रशंसकऽ के जुटान म॑ मई २०२६ म॑ काठमांडू म॑ सरकारी, अकादमी आरू सलाहकारऽ के इंजीनियर शामिल छेलै ।फोटो: लिसा चोएग्याल

किछु तैयारी के यात्रा के बाद 1991 में रिचर्ड भवन महानिदेशक के बगल में बाबर महल में एकटा कार्यालय में बसलाह. हुनकऽ अविचारित काम नै छेलै भूकंपीय खतरा के मानचित्रण आरू जोखिम के आकलन ताकि राष्ट्रीय भवन संहिता तैयार करी क॑ लागू करलऽ जाय सक॑ ।

ओ लिखैत छथि : ‘हम सब भूकंप के लेल डिजाइन के पहलू स बहुत बेसी उपलब्ध करौलहुं। वैकल्पिक निर्माण सामग्री आ प्रौद्योगिकी के विकास में पूरा नेपाल में 55 ठेठ घर के इन्वेंट्री शामिल छल।'

रिचर्ड केरऽ नेपाली विशेषज्ञऽ के टीम नेपाल केरऽ विशिष्ट परिस्थिति के अनुरूप बिल्डिंग कोड प॑ काम करै लेली तैयार होय गेलै । अधिकांश घर स्वनिर्मित या स्थानीय रूप सं बिना राजमिस्त्री या इंजीनियर के बनल छल, ताहि लेल संहिता में आम भवन प्रकार के लेल अनिवार्य नियम आ कम औपचारिक संरचना के लेल विस्तृत दिशा निर्देश शामिल छल.

पहिल प्रशिक्षण कार्यशाला 1993 मे धरान मे सरकारी निरीक्षक लेल आयोजित भेल छल। फोटो : रिचर्ड शार्प

ई कोड क॑ प्रोफेशनली डिजाइन करलऽ गेलऽ आधुनिक भवन आरू नया हाई राइज लेली भी प्रासंगिकता होना चाहियऽ छेलै । जल्दिये ई बात साफ होय गेलै कि सरकारी अधिकारी आरू निरीक्षकऽ के थोक म॑ एकरऽ सिफारिश क॑ प्रभावी ढंग स॑ लागू करै के क्षमता के कमी छै, ई लेली टीम फेर स॑ मूल बात प॑ चली गेलै ।

पहिल प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम धरान मे 1993 मे भेल छल ।आगू एनएसईटी क स्थापना करय वाला हुनकर टीम मे स एक आमोद दीक्षित बतौलथि जे सरकारी आ स्थानीय दुनू तरहक विचार प्रक्रिया मे सांस्कृतिक समुद्र-परिवर्तन क आवश्यकता अछि।

ओ कहलनि जे, रिचर्ड शार्प के बारे में जे एतेक प्रेरणादायक छल ओ छल जे ओ हमरा सब के नेपाल विशिष्ट समाधान के अपना लेल काज करय लेल प्रोत्साहित केलनि, कहियो हमरा सब के डिक्टेट नै केलनि।हुनकर नेतृत्व में हमरा सब के आत्मविश्वास बढ़ल, मुदा हुनकर अंतर्दृष्टि आ अनुभव के बिना हम सब कहियो ओतय नहि पहुंच सकितहुं।”

मंत्र

रिचर्ड शार्प केरऽ मंत्र दाता केरऽ निर्भरता के उल्टा छेलै आरू अपनऽ सहयोगी केरऽ कौशल क॑ पहचानी रहलऽ छेलै । ओ कहैत छलाह, “अहाँ नेपाली अभियंता सब स्वयं क सकैत छी, आ हम सब अहाँक सहयोग आ मार्गदर्शन करब।”

बिल्डिंग कोड परियोजना के अंतिम सप्ताह में रिचर्ड नेपाल टीम के संग मिल क गति के कायम रखबाक लेल एकटा विद्वान समाज के गठन केलक, आ ओ सब केलक। फंडिंग मिललै आरू एनएसईटी केरऽ जन्म होय गेलै, जेकरऽ विधान न्यूजीलैंड सोसाइटी फॉर अर्थक्वेक इंजीनियरिंग केरऽ विधान प॑ आधारित छेलै ।

2010 में काठमांडू के याक एंड येती होटल के झूमर के नीचा एनएसईटी आ संयुक्त राष्ट्र के तरफ सं एक संग आनल गेल अंतर्राष्ट्रीय भूकंप विशेषज्ञ के संग एकटा पैघ सम्मेलन में भाग लेनिहार दर्शक में हम छलहुं. कीवी टेलीविजन हस्ती बॉब पार्कर, जे आब क्राइस्टचर्च के मेयर छथि, के मुख्य वक्ता के रूप में आमंत्रित कायल गेल छल.

शहर केरऽ कहानी क॑ नाटकीय रूप स॑ दोबारा बतैतें हुअ॑ कि कोना हुनी हाल केरऽ मैग्नीट्यूड ७.१ भूकंप स॑ शून्य जानलेवा के साथ बचलै, करिश्माई मेयर बॉब न॑ एकरऽ अवधि के ४० सेकंड लेली अपनऽ लेक्चरर प॑ टक्कर मारतें हुअ॑ सभा क॑ बिजली पैदा करी देलकै । जेना सदाक लेल। घर घुरलाक किछुए दिनक बाद क्राइस्टचर्च एतेक भाग्यशाली नहि छल । दोसर पैघ झटका मे 22 फरवरी 2011 कए 185 लोक क मौत भ गेल छल, जाहि मे शहर तबाह भ गेल छल।

रिचर्ड शार्प न॑ कीवी स्ट्रक्चरल इंजीनियरिंग टीम के नेतृत्व करलकै जे 2015 म॑ मंत्री केरऽ आग्रह के जवाब देलकै । मई म॑ एशिया न्यूजीलैंड फाउंडेशन केरऽ सहयोग स॑ आयोजित एगो सेमिनार म॑ बोलै लेली हुनी वापस काठमांडू पहुँचलऽ छेलै । हुनक अनुयायी, सरकारी, शिक्षा आ परामर्श क्षेत्रक इंजीनियर, आब प्रतिष्ठित धूसर बूढ़ जे नेपाल केँ आकार देने छलाह आ जे हुनका सर्वोच्च सम्मान मे रखैत छथि, द्वारा आयोजित भोजन मे भेंट भेल ।

नेवी रंगक सुरुचिपूर्ण जैकेट में रिचर्ड प्रशंसा पत्रक बीच सं लजा गेलाह, जखन हम सब बुफे में अपना कें मदद केलहुं. प्रशंसा पर शर्मिंदगी के बावजूद रिचर्ड केरऽ जुनून आरू ज्ञान अदम्य छेलै, कैन्हेंकि हम्मं॑ भविष्य केरऽ खतरा के सामना करै लेली दूरस्थ अस्पताल, स्कूल आरू अन्य सार्वजनिक भवन जेना कि सुप्रीम कोर्ट आरू सिंघा दरबार जैसनऽ आइसोलेट आइसोलेट करै लेली एनएसईटी लेली विभिन्न फंडिंग के अवसरऽ के चर्चा करलियै । एनएसईटी हाल ही म॑ भूटान आरू ओकरा स॑ बाहर के क्षेत्र म॑ अपनऽ विशेषज्ञता साझा करी रहलऽ छै ।

हुनी कहलकै, 'अभी एगो बहुत रोचक स्थिति छै, जेकरा मँ भारत नँ अपनौ भूकंप संहिता मँ हाल मँ संशोधन क वापस ल॑ लेलकै, कैन्हेंकि अनुमानित लागत के चलतें जनता के आक्रोश छै । “ई अपडेट में वैह तकनीक आ दृष्टिकोण के प्रयोग करबाक प्रस्ताव छल जे नेपाल तीस साल स बेसी पहिने हमर सबहक परियोजना में डिजाइन बल आ भूकंपीय जोनिंग सेट केने छल।अहाँ कहि सकैत छी जे भारत नेपाल के पकड़ि रहल अछि।”

title: Nepal Strengthens Workplace Health and Safety Through Chemical Risk Prevention - fundsforNGOs News
description: Nepal Strengthens Workplace Health and Safety Through Chemical Risk Prevention  fundsforNGOs News
publisher.title: fundsforNGOs News
full_article:
Nepal is strengthening efforts to protect workers from hazardous chemical exposure by improving prevention, national coordination and workplace risk management. The initiative comes as the use of potentially dangerous chemicals increases across agriculture, manufacturing, construction, healthcare and other important sectors.

Although Nepal has made progress in developing its occupational safety and health framework, significant challenges remain. These include gaps in institutional coordination, enforcement, workplace chemical risk assessment, information sharing and technical capacity.

The International Labour Organization and Nepal’s Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment organised a national policy dialogue in Kathmandu to identify practical measures for safer chemical management and healthier workplaces. The event brought together government institutions, employers’ and workers’ organisations, industry representatives, technical specialists and development partners.

The dialogue formed part of an ILO project focused on integrating occupational safety and health into the implementation of the Global Framework on Chemicals. The project is supported by Germany’s Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety and implemented through the ILO’s Safety and Health for All programme.

The project seeks to strengthen occupational safety and health systems while promoting the environmentally sound management of chemicals and waste. Its broader objective is to reduce chemical-related risks for workers, workplaces and surrounding communities.

Participants reviewed Nepal’s existing laws, policies and institutional arrangements for managing chemicals and protecting occupational health. They also examined how government agencies, employers and workers could coordinate more effectively at national and workplace levels.

International labour standards and chemical safety practices were central to the discussions. Participants considered the Global Framework on Chemicals, relevant ILO conventions and guidance, and the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals.

The Globally Harmonized System provides a standard approach for classifying chemical hazards and communicating risks through labels and safety information. Stronger implementation could help workers and employers identify dangerous substances, understand exposure risks and take appropriate precautions.

The dialogue emphasised the importance of social dialogue and cooperation among governments, employers and workers. This tripartite approach can help ensure that future chemical safety policies reflect workplace realities and provide practical protections for employees across different industries.

A major objective was to move beyond identifying policy and implementation gaps and define coordinated actions. Discussions focused on strengthening legislation, improving institutional responsibilities, expanding workplace chemical risk management and building technical knowledge.

Participants also examined the need for stronger awareness among employers and workers. Effective chemical safety requires people handling hazardous materials to understand correct storage, labelling, transportation, use and disposal procedures, as well as the health effects associated with exposure.

The proposed approach prioritises prevention at the source. Wherever possible, hazardous chemicals should be eliminated or replaced with safer alternatives. When substitution is not feasible, workplaces should introduce engineering controls and safe work systems to reduce the possibility of exposure.

Personal protective equipment should serve as the final layer of protection rather than the primary safety measure. This approach recognises that gloves, respirators and protective clothing cannot replace effective hazard elimination, equipment design, ventilation and safe operating procedures.

Participants identified priority areas for future action, including improved chemical safety governance, clearer institutional responsibilities, stronger data collection and better cooperation among relevant agencies and social partners. Building national and workplace-level technical capacity was also recognised as essential.

The recommendations are expected to support Nepal’s implementation of the Global Framework on Chemicals. They may also guide future policy development, institutional strengthening, training programmes and workplace prevention measures.

By placing worker protection at the centre of chemical management, Nepal aims to reduce occupational exposure, prevent workplace illnesses and injuries, and create healthier working environments. Continued cooperation among government, employers, workers and development partners will be critical to translating the dialogue’s recommendations into effective action.
translated:
नेपाल रोकथाम, राष्ट्रीय समन्वय आ कार्यस्थल जोखिम प्रबंधन मे सुधार क श्रमिकक कें खतरनाक रासायनिक संपर्क सं बचाव कें प्रयास मजबूत कयर रहल छै. ई पहल ऐन्हऽ समय म॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छै जब॑ कृषि, निर्माण, निर्माण, स्वास्थ्य सेवा आरू अन्य महत्वपूर्ण क्षेत्रऽ म॑ संभावित खतरनाक रसायनऽ के इस्तेमाल बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ।

यद्यपि नेपाल अपन व्यावसायिक सुरक्षा आ स्वास्थ्य ढाँचा के विकास मे प्रगति केलक अछि, मुदा महत्वपूर्ण चुनौती एखनो अछि । अइ मे संस्थागत समन्वय, प्रवर्तन, कार्यस्थल पर रासायनिक जोखिम आकलन, सूचना साझा करनाय आ तकनीकी क्षमता मे अंतराल शामिल छै.

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय श्रम संगठन आ नेपालक युवा, श्रम तथा रोजगार मन्त्रालय काठमाण्डौमे राष्ट्रिय नीति संवादक आयोजन कए सुरक्षित रासायनिक प्रबंधन आ स्वस्थ कार्यस्थलके लेल व्यावहारिक उपायके पहिचान केलक । ई आयोजन म॑ सरकारी संस्थान, नियोक्ता आरू मजदूर संगठन, उद्योग प्रतिनिधि, तकनीकी विशेषज्ञ आरू विकास भागीदार सब क॑ एक साथ लानलऽ गेलै ।

इ संवाद आईएलओ कें एकटा परियोजना कें हिस्सा बनल जे व्यावसायिक सुरक्षा आ स्वास्थ्य कें रसायन पर वैश्विक ढाँचा कें क्रियान्वयन मे एकीकृत करय पर केंद्रित छल. ई परियोजना क॑ जर्मनी केरऽ संघीय पर्यावरण, जलवायु कार्रवाई, प्रकृति संरक्षण आरू परमाणु सुरक्षा मंत्रालय द्वारा समर्थित करलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू आईएलओ केरऽ सब लेली सुरक्षा आरू स्वास्थ्य कार्यक्रम के माध्यम स॑ लागू करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

इ परियोजना व्यावसायिक सुरक्षा आ स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली कें मजबूत करय कें कोशिश करय छै आ संगहि रसायन आ अपशिष्ट कें पर्यावरणीय रूप सं सही प्रबंधन कें बढ़ावा देवय कें कोशिश करय छै. एकर व्यापक उद्देश्य श्रमिकक, कार्यस्थल आ आसपास कें समुदायक कें लेल रसायन सं संबंधित जोखिम कें कम करनाय छै.

प्रतिभागी सब नेपाल के मौजूदा कानून, नीति आ रसायन के प्रबंधन आ व्यावसायिक स्वास्थ्य के रक्षा के लेल संस्थागत व्यवस्था के समीक्षा केलनि। ओ सब इहो जांच केलनि जे सरकारी एजेंसी, नियोक्ता आ मजदूर राष्ट्रीय आ कार्यस्थल स्तर पर कोना बेसी प्रभावी ढंग सं समन्वय क सकैत अछि.

अंतर्राष्ट्रीय श्रम मानक आ रासायनिक सुरक्षा प्रथा एहि चर्चा मे केंद्रीय छल । प्रतिभागियक न॑ रसायनऽ प॑ वैश्विक रूपरेखा, प्रासंगिक आईएलओ सम्मेलन आरू मार्गदर्शन, आरू रसायनऽ के वर्गीकरण आरू लेबलिंग केरऽ वैश्विक सामंजस्यपूर्ण प्रणाली प॑ विचार करलकै ।

वैश्विक रूप सं सामंजस्यपूर्ण प्रणाली रासायनिक खतरा कें वर्गीकरण आ लेबल आ सुरक्षा जानकारी कें माध्यम सं जोखिम कें संप्रेषण कें लेल एकटा मानक दृष्टिकोण प्रदान करयत छै. मजबूत कार्यान्वयन श्रमिक आ नियोक्ता कें खतरनाक पदार्थक कें पहचान करय, संपर्क मे आवय कें जोखिम कें समझय आ उचित सावधानी लेवय मे मदद कयर सकय छै.

संवाद मे सरकार, नियोक्ता आ मजदूर के बीच सामाजिक संवाद आ सहयोग के महत्व पर जोर देल गेल। इ त्रिपक्षीय दृष्टिकोण इ सुनिश्चित करय मे मदद कयर सकय छै की भविष्य कें रासायनिक सुरक्षा नीतियक कार्यस्थल कें वास्तविकताक कें प्रतिबिंबित करय आ विभिन्न उद्योगक मे कर्मचारीक कें लेल व्यावहारिक सुरक्षा प्रदान करय सकय छै.

एकटा प्रमुख उद्देश्य नीति आ कार्यान्वयन अंतराल कें पहचान करय सं आगू बढ़नाय आ समन्वित कार्यवाही कें परिभाषित करनाय छल. चर्चा कानून कें मजबूत करनाय, संस्थागत जिम्मेदारियक मे सुधार, कार्यस्थल पर रासायनिक जोखिम प्रबंधन कें विस्तार आ तकनीकी ज्ञान कें निर्माण पर केंद्रित छल.

प्रतिभागी सब नियोक्ता आ मजदूर के बीच मजबूत जागरूकता के आवश्यकता के सेहो जांच केलनि। प्रभावी रासायनिक सुरक्षा कें लेल खतरनाक सामग्री कें संभालएय वाला लोगक कें सही भंडारण, लेबलिंग, परिवहन, उपयोग आ निपटान प्रक्रियाक कें संग-संग एक्सपोजर सं जुड़ल स्वास्थ्य प्रभावक कें समझनाय आवश्यक छै.

प्रस्तावित दृष्टिकोण स्रोत पर रोकथाम कें प्राथमिकता देयत छै. जत संभव होएयत खतरनाक रसायन कें समाप्त कैल जेबाक चाही या सुरक्षित विकल्पक कें साथ बदलल जेबाक चाही. जखन प्रतिस्थापन संभव नहि होयत छै, तखन कार्यस्थल पर इंजीनियरिंग नियंत्रण आ सुरक्षित कार्य प्रणाली कें शुरूआत करबाक चाही, ताकि एक्सपोजर कें संभावना कम भ सकय.

व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षा उपकरणक कें प्राथमिक सुरक्षा उपाय कें बजाय सुरक्षा कें अंतिम परत कें रूप मे काज करबाक चाही. इ दृष्टिकोण इ बात कें पहचान करएयत छै की दस्ताना, श्वसन यंत्र आ सुरक्षात्मक कपड़ा प्रभावी खतरा उन्मूलन, उपकरणक कें डिजाइन, हवादार आ सुरक्षित संचालन प्रक्रियाक कें जगह नहि ल सकएय छै.

प्रतिभागियक भविष्य मे कार्रवाई कें लेल प्राथमिकता क्षेत्रक कें पहचान करलकय, जइ मे बेहतर रासायनिक सुरक्षा शासन, स्पष्ट संस्थागत जिम्मेदारियक, मजबूत आंकड़ा संग्रहण आ संबंधित एजेंसियॉ आ सामाजिक भागीदारक कें बीच बेहतर सहयोग शामिल छै. राष्ट्रीय आ कार्यस्थल स्तर कें तकनीकी क्षमता कें निर्माण कें सेहो आवश्यक मानल गेलय.

एहि सिफारिश स नेपाल कए रसायन पर वैश्विक ढाँचा कए लागू करबा मे सहयोग भेटबाक उम्मीद अछि। इ भविष्य कें नीति विकास, संस्थागत मजबूती, प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम आ कार्यस्थल पर रोकथाम कें उपायक कें मार्गदर्शन सेहो कयर सकय छै.

श्रमिक संरक्षण के रसायन प्रबंधन के केंद्र में राखि नेपाल के उद्देश्य व्यावसायिक संपर्क कम करब, कार्यस्थल पर बीमारी आ चोट के रोकब, आ स्वस्थ कार्य वातावरण बनाबय के अछि। संवाद कें सिफारिशक कें प्रभावी कार्यवाही मे बदलय कें लेल सरकार, नियोक्ता, मजदूर आ विकास भागीदारक कें बीच निरंतर सहयोग महत्वपूर्ण होयत.
